tuning.decision: GroupNorm (8 groups) with SGD lr=0.05 and K=20 local steps provides strictly monotonic post-round-15 convergence (AUC 0.7285 -> 0.7770 -> 0.8273 -> 0.8510) and outperforms FedAvg-SGD (0.7845) by +0.0665 without BN client drift collapse.

temporal.split_note: A chronological split is not possible because frame.time has no date (99.2% NaNs under numeric parsing); a session-disjoint split via GroupShuffleSplit on (ip.src_host, ip.dst_host, tcp.stream) is used instead.

session-disjoint.split_note: A chronological split is not possible because frame.time has no date (99.2% NaNs under numeric parsing); a session-disjoint split via GroupShuffleSplit on (ip.src_host, ip.dst_host, tcp.stream) is used instead.

ablation_benchmarks.explanation: In the 3,000 test holdout samples, only 188 unique feature vectors exist (6.27%) due to discrete protocol header fields. Because discrete protocol features map multiple network connections to identical categorical/integer representations, different random seeds produce identical test predictions, explaining identical classifications across seeds.

scratch_on_target.description: Same architecture trained from random init on the same 20% target split (no source pre-training); reference for the fine-tuned row

cross_dataset_transfer.source_model: centrally trained on the shared-feature subset (not the FL checkpoint)
cross_dataset_transfer.feature_space_note: Edge-IIoTset is packet-level; WUSTL-IIoT-2021 is flow-level. Only 3 semantically shared features exist; zero-shot transfer is reported as a negative result.

energy_consumption.notes: Estimated via CPU TDP proxy: Energy (J) = Time (s) x TDP (W)

session-disjoint.split_note: A chronological split is not possible because frame.time has no date (99.2% NaNs under numeric parsing). Split is session-disjoint via GroupShuffleSplit(80/20) on (ip.src_host, ip.dst_host, stream/ports), ensuring zero session overlap.

string_one_hot.description: One-hot encoded string representation (original repository recipe)
string_one_hot.finding: Achieves ~1.0 ROC-AUC (99.98% accuracy) purely by memorizing the string formatting anomaly ('0' for normal vs '0.0' for attack).

numeric_parsed.finding: Collapses both '0' and '0.0' to identical 0.0, destroying the artifact and dropping ROC-AUC to chance (~0.50).
